correctness.rationale: Checked the mechanical threshold argument (RESULT.md, lines 21–52) independently. In phases 0<=t<1, the cumulative ones through j bits are floor(t+j alpha). Each j from 1 through n gives exactly one threshold ceil(j alpha)-j alpha; irrationality makes them interior and pairwise distinct. The half-open intervals give the common Sturmian language by the dense irrational orbit, and the endpoint choices of lower/upper coding give values already realized on one side. Moving through the thresholds in phase order strictly increases the input lexicographically: for j<n the change is 01 to 10 in positions j-1,j (zero-based), and for j=n only the last bit changes 0 to 1. At j<n the changed pair is erased down to its common zero exactly when the prefix preceding the pair contains no 1; then both outputs coincide, including the common appended 1. Otherwise the first 1 is removed from the common prefix and the change survives as a strict increase. A final-bit change also gives a strict increase, including the case with no earlier 1. At the threshold the prefix count equals ceil(j alpha)-1, so mergers occur exactly at the internal labels j<=floor(1/alpha). Nondecreasing image order rules out any further loss from nonadjacent collisions. Thus the stated defect is exactly min(n-1,floor(1/alpha)); n=1 has two images and the empty word has one. The proof is for frequency of 1 and one application only. The two finite factor sources and recorded five PASS lines were inspected, not executed or used to justify the universal claim.

value.rationale: This computes an invariant introduced for factor languages precisely where the motivating paper invites Sturmian work. It turns a bounded-loss statement into an exact slope-sensitive crossover: two images up to n=floor(1/alpha)+1, then linear growth with known deficit. Neither classical factor complexity nor a qualitative deficit bound gives that profile. It is a natural one-step benchmark independent of the later iterate extension.
